articles.title: Google Health is here, but a lot of people want their Fitbit app back instead
articles.summary: Google Health has officially replaced the Fitbit app, leaving many users frustrated with the new app’s design and Google’s AI health coach.
articles.body: The Fitbit app is no more. Along with the launch of the new Fitbit Air (which you can expect a full review of once we’ve spent more time with it), Google has officially replaced it with Google Health, as previously announced, and many of the responses we’ve seen so far are full of confusion, frustration, and requests to get the old app back. One post on Reddit calls out a common issue, saying, “I can’t even completely fill up my home screen. They only have 2 large tiles available and I can’t just scroll down to see everything.” The landing page has a small section up top showing steps and some other basic stats, but part of the app’s main page is now reserved for recent activity updates and chatty notes from Google’s AI health coach. [Media: The AI didn’t have much to say to me, but for my senior editor, Richard Lawler, it started a conversation about today’s plans that he wasn’t quite ready to have with a chatbot. [Image: Not everyone is annoyed by the AI bot however, with one person commenting, “When I ask it to design a moderate workout using my office gym equipment, circuit style, I usually end up feeling great afterwards.” Another person called it “quite a helpful feature,” showing how they were able to update their sleep log with a missed session by chatting with the AI bot. Another user said, “This graphic UI looks like something an 8 year old would make,” while someone else complained, “Why must I now scroll through paragraphs of AI slop on every tab before I can actually see my activities and data? I don’t want or need to read platitudes about my 15 minute walk to the grocery store. I want to see my stats from my morning run.” One post on Google’s help center sums things up, saying, “This app is a huge disappointment and a total time drain to get minimal results. How can I get back to using what worked?!” Many others were in agreement, with one reply saying, “it’s no longer a genuine fitness app.” On Google’s blog post, its sample image shows a version of the Today screen with all of the information and an AI chat that we couldn’t get to show up, but did appear for some users. There doesn’t seem to be any way to remove the Ask Coach / activity window that takes up so much of the screen, but the bot can be disabled from within the new app’s Feature Privacy Controls. [Image: [Image: [Image: Even though I knew the switch to Google Health was coming, I was still disoriented for the first several minutes after opening the app this morning. If you want to see more of your stats and health tracking data, you have to either swipe left in the small top box on the “Today” page or tab over to the “Health” page. To find logs for my rowing workouts that I had stored in the old Fitbit app, I had to go into “Health,” then down to the “Fitness” section in “Focus areas,” where my logs were viewable under “Exercise days.” In the old Fitbit app, I could see the “Exercise days” block by just scrolling down on the app’s main “Today” page. According to a support page, if you have a supported wearable connected, Google Health shows two additional tabs for Fitness and Sleep that would make things easier, but before the redesign, I didn’t need those. While Google’s Rishi Chandra told The Verge earlier this month that Google Health will eventually support third-party wearables, my Nothing Watch Pro 3 currently isn’t enough to unlock those two extra tabs.

articles.title: A week with Googlebooks: four notes from our testing so far
articles.summary: We’ve been testing Googlebook laptops from Dell, Lenovo, Asus, Acer, and HP all week — all five launch offerings — and we already have many thoughts about Google’s new operating system.
articles.body: Google’s new operating system is off to a rocky start. The five newly launched Googlebook laptops have hardware that ranges from great to excellent, but the software in its current state is the weak point. There are four of us on staff at The Verge actively testing Googlebooks and, frankly, our internal Slack discussions have been mostly filled with collective venting of frustrations, disappointments, and bewilderment. The promise of Googlebooks as a fresh and smartly designed alternative to Windows or Mac for Android phone owners sounds great, but there’s more than just a few kinks and quirks to work out. Some of its issues and challenges in the road ahead are systemic to Android. While we’re actively testing each and every Googlebook from all of Google’s partner OEMs, we thought we’d come together and share a glimpse of where our heads are at with these new laptops. This should be better than ChromeOS, but right now it feels worse [Image: Why does this Clear all button exist? Why can’t you swipe between active desktops or move windows between them? And why wasn’t that ready on day one? While a lot of my thoughts are well documented in our initial hands-on article, I keep coming back to what a Google rep told me at the Googlebook launch preview: Replacing ChromeOS with Android will allow for much faster development. That’s great, but why does Googlebook OS feel like a bit of a set back from ChromeOS at launch? It shares some of ChromeOS’ flaws, like not allowing you to run Chrome with separate Google accounts. And many Android apps feel as clunky to run on a Googlebook as they did on ChromeOS. (Google even put Android’s navigation buttons on the Googlebook keyboard — seemingly in part as a fallback option for misbehaving apps.) Every day I come across new oddities in any of the three Googlebooks I’m testing. The Signal Android app linked to my phone with ease, but I have to hit Ctrl+Enter to send messages and can’t highlight text — clicking and dragging scrolls up and down instead. Photoshop and Lightroom are passable for the simplest image editing, but I’d take a cheap Windows laptop with the proper desktop apps over these mobile-first versions. You can’t drag and drop windows to other virtual desktops, and scrolling to the left of your desktops reveals a Clear All button that just kills all your apps at once. That’s straight out of the app switcher from Android on phones, but if I’m closing all apps at once on a laptop I’m either rebooting or shutting down. Even something as simple as installing the progressive web app version of Slack isn’t working properly. So who should I be mad at? Slack or Google? If I bought one of these Googlebooks I’d be mad at myself for being a paying beta tester for Google. I know that’s often the case for early adopters on a new OS, but these days I have less time and patience than when I bought my T-Mobile G1 / HTC Dream, Nexus 7, etc. There’s something cool here for sure with Googlebooks, but we need that “faster” development to go into warp speed. — Antonio G. Di Benedetto, currently testing the HP Googlebook 14, Lenovo Googlebook 15, and Acer Googlebook 14 Google has a big, big developer problem [Image: Streaming apps like Crunchyroll are basically tablet apps. The keyboard can’t pause or rewind, and you have to click or touch the screen for those playback controls. One of the reasons Googlebooks exist is that Android has become a mature, useful platform across a lot of screen sizes. It’s true: Android now works relatively well on your phone, tablet, TV, even your car. The apps are another story. Over and over in my testing so far, I’ve been amazed at the number of apps that seem to have no idea what to do with a Googlebook. Take Netflix, for instance, which was one of the first apps I downloaded because I have some travel coming up and I’m psyched to finally be able to download movies for plane rides. The app works well enough, I suppose (and it does download movies!) but it launches as a full-screen, tablet-style version of the app. Basically every streaming app does so. If you hover over the top bar, the windowing option appears, but none of that is obvious. And launching and windowing app after app gets tiresome. There are a few apps that are properly optimized for Googlebooks, and they make the device feel more like a proper laptop. But even they have some problems: many do that weird thing where they don’t show the app content when you’re resizing the window, for instance, which feels broken on a laptop. Even some of Google’s own apps do this, while others, like YouTube and Messages, scale more naturally. Some apps respond naturally to the keyboard and mouse; others don’t. Virtually everything is better optimized for a touchscreen. A note to developers: If I can’t pause the movie by whacking the space bar, your app doesn’t work with keyboards. For the most part, I actually like the Android-ification of Google’s laptop strategy. Connecting deeply to your phone, running and syncing all your apps, even some of the phone-style interface decisions make sense to me. But just about every time I open an app, my Googlebook starts to seem like an Android tablet pretending to be a laptop. (And don’t forget: nobody has ever really wanted Android tablets.) Google’s going to need developers to get with the program, or it’ll never be more than that. — David Pierce, currently testing the Dell XPS Googlebook Linux apps (probably) can’t save Googlebook OS [Image: Apps in the Googlebook’s Linux virtual machine don’t show up in the taskbar or app tray. A string of little annoyances has chipped away at my hopes for the new Googlebooks over the last few days. Some are more frustrating than others — losing a normal Caps Lock key isn’t a deal breaker, but getting stuck with only mobile browsers just might be. Android app compatibility seems to always be a roll of the dice, and so far Linux apps don’t seem like a viable alternative. Slack was one of the first apps I tried installing from the Play Store, but it ended up being the mobile app awkwardly resized for a larger screen. So, I tried installing the Linux version of Slack through the Debian virtual machine that lives in the Googlebook’s Terminal app. I got it working, along with GIMP and Steam. But the big catch is that anything you install on the virtual machine only lives there. So, none of those apps have app drawer icons like my Android apps, and they don’t pop up in my taskbar when they’re running. I have to manually switch my mouse and keyboard between the VM and the rest of Googlebook OS, which makes jumping between Linux and Android apps slow and awkward. Since the Linux and Android apps are running in different environments, they don’t automatically share files or clipboard content, either. I’ll have a dedicated write-up on the Googlebook gaming experience later, but the virtual machine hasn’t been great for that, either. I got Steam running, but the games I’ve tried (none of which are particularly resource-hungry) have been too laggy to be playable. I’ve liked some parts of the Googlebook so far, but it’s hard to appreciate them when friction keeps popping up from Android and Linux apps alike. — Stevie Bonifield, currently testing the Asus Googlebook 14 The best bit of Googlebooks only works half the time [Image: The Files app gives you quick access to what’s on your paired Android phone. But opening or transferring those files is anything but “quick.” The obvious selling point of the Googlebook, for me at least, has always been the “seamless” Android integration. And I’ve had a few moments this week when my phone and laptop have come together in a truly delightful way: replying to a WhatsApp message directly from the notification on the Googlebook; dipping into an app cast from my phone to quickly use it without reaching for my pocket; opening Quick Share to move files between the two devices in seconds. But even here, so much of the experience right now sucks. My phone connection drops in and out from the laptop, and I can’t for the life of me figure out how to connect a second phone or tablet. I used Quick Share for file transfer because using the Files app to browse the phone’s drive is painfully slow, taking minutes to open or transfer a single photo. Opening a notification to the phone-cast version of an app when you have it installed natively will never stop feeling awkward. And some apps cast terribly anyway: Bluesky renders text illegibly; my banking app won’t cast for security reasons; and my credit card one won’t because it just breaks. Seamless, this is not. It’ll get better, I hope. It has to get better. When the Android integration works, it feels a little bit like magic. But that’s only because it happens so rarely — Google needs to make this reliable enough that it feels mundane instead. — Dominic Preston, currently testing the Asus Googlebook 14 and HP Googlebook 14

articles.title: Aamrapali Dubey’s sister Aanchal slams Gullu and Mahhi Vij over ‘Motu Patlu and Football’ body-shaming remarks
articles.summary: In the previous episode of Bigg Boss 20 a heated argument took place during a task between Gullu and Bhojpuri Star Aamrapali Dubey.
articles.body: In the previous episode of Bigg Boss 20 a heated argument took place during a task between Gullu and Bhojpuri Star Aamrapali Dubey. The argument gradually took an unpleasant turn when Gullu compared Aamrapali and Love’s jodi to that of ‘Motu Patlu’s cartoon characters. The remark has now drawn criticism from Aamrapali’s sister, Aanchal, who strongly condemned the comments and questioned why body shaming continues to be used during disagreements and why isn’t it being pointed out?Slamming the remarks, Aanchal emphasised that a person’s physical appearance should never become a subject of ridicule, particularly when the discussion has nothing to do with their performances or working abilities. She also called out Mahhi Vij, referring to her previous remarks about Aamrapali, in which she allegedly called the actress a ‘football’ and made other derogatory comments about her appearance and profession.Expressing her disappointment, Aanchal took to her Instagram story and stated, “Why is it so easy for Mahhi Vij and Gullu to body shame Aamrapali (my sister) and get away with it? Body shaming is never okay. A person’s body should never be the subject of ridicule, especially when their body of work speaks for itself. No matter what shape or size Aamrapali has been, she has always been a hit in the industry, winning hearts with her talent and performances. Body shaming is not an achievement. Agar fight dena hai toh dignified tarike se dona.. jab Aamrapali ke against kuch point nahi mila toh ye remarks shuru kar diye? Your body of work is what truly matters. And Aamrapali’s work speaks louder than any personal remarks ever could. I and our family are proud of my sister.”Furthermore, Aamrapali’s team was also seen asking the makers if this topic will be raised on weekend ka vaar or no.The post read, “Chota Bheem, Indumati and Chutki ke baare mein Weekend ke Vaar par baat hui thi.. articles.title: Amazon’s new Kindles appear to have a light leak problem
articles.summary: Reddit users are reporting shadows and visible LEDs around screen edge of new Kindles.
articles.body: Some users are reporting that the new Kindles have a light leak issue that is especially apparent when using dark mode. The latest base-model Kindles have a flush bezel that gives them a sleek appearance and looks great… as long as you keep the lights on. But things can change once you turn down the lights and turn up the brightness on the e-reader. In some cases, users see shadows around the edges of the screen, or even visible LED strips. The issue appears to affect both the plastic and aluminum models in all colors. Some minor glowing around the edges might be a byproduct of the combination of front lighting and a flush screen. But Reddit users say images shared there show something more dramatic that appears to be a defect. [Media: Good e-Reader says that Amazon is aware of the issue and has confirmed that a manufacturing issue may have led to defects in the current batch of Kindles. When contacted by The Verge, Amazon spokesperson Katie Condon said, “In certain, highly specific conditions, such as using dark mode at a higher brightness settings in a dark environment, customers may see a subtle glow on the edge of the display on devices with colored bezels. This can be mitigated by adjusting the front light to a lower level.” Update October 9th, 2026: Added statement from Amazon.

articles.body: Amazon has the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra in black with 256GB of storage discounted to $949.99, a healthy discount from its usual price of $1,399.99. This phone’s standout feature is the adjustable privacy display, which can hide your entire screen, or just portions of it, from onlookers and strangers. It doesn’t meaningfully hurt the screen’s performance otherwise, and it’s only noticeable at steep angles, and it includes a built-in stylus for writing or drawing. [Product: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra | Even beyond the privacy display, the S26 Ultra is an impressive flagship phone for mobile enthusiasts. The upgraded camera hardware makes a big difference when it comes to photo quality, particularly in low lighting conditions. For better or worse, it’s still a sizable phone, with a 6.9-inch AMOLED display, but it’s slimmer and more comfortable than the S25 Ultra. Read our Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra review.

articles.title: Google teases Fitbit Edge launch next week
articles.summary: Google is getting ready to launch its rumored fitness tracker, the Fitbit Edge, on October 12th.
articles.body: It looks like Google is getting ready to take the wraps off its rumored Fitbit Edge next Monday. In a post on X, Google posted a picture of what appears to be the side of the fitness tracker, with the caption: “Get an Edge on your health. 10.12.26.” A trove of Fitbit Edge leaks has surfaced over the past couple of weeks. So far, details shared by Dealabs and Android Headlines suggest that the upcoming device could feature a 1.34-inch always-on OLED touchscreen, built-in GPS, and several other sensors, including an accelerometer, barometer, altimeter, and gyroscope. It may also come with optical sensors for measuring heart rate and blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) and electrical sensors for capturing ECGs. [Image: A leaked image that appears to show the Fitbit Edge. As reported by Dealabs, the tracker may also be able to notify wearers about potential atrial fibrillation and irregular heart rhythms. The Fitbit Edge is rumored to come with a replaceable lithium-ion battery with up to seven days of battery life. Rumors suggest that it could cost around $180 in the US when it launches next week.

articles.title: Long live the mechanical keyboard | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Keychron made a name for itself after launching on Kickstarter in 2017. Today, it offers the value K2 model as well as a variety of other versions, including one with an all-wood body.
articles.body:
For a writer, the mechanical keyboard is a beautiful thing. It’s certainly not necessary for everyone, but a well-designed mechanical keyboard can turn a tedious day of typing into an aesthetically pleasing experience.

Given that most of my days involve sitting at a desk for hours, having a keyboard that I enjoy using is a necessity. I first got a mechanical keyboard about two years ago — the Keychron K2 — and I’ve never looked back.

Keychron is one of the most prominent brands within the mechanical keyboard industry, having made a name for itself after initially launching via Kickstarter back in 2017. The company has since produced dozens of different keyboards (as well as keypads) and a variety of mouse models .

Unlike other electronics, there isn’t a whole lot to owning a mechanical keyboard. The simplicity is part of the appeal. You unbox them, set them up (the K2 comes with little tilt legs that give you a slightly better angle from which to type), and plug them in.

From here, you have a couple of different options. The K2 comes with a simple USB cable, but there’s also an option for Bluetooth connection. If you value a clean, minimalist workspace, Bluetooth is probably the way to go.

While I am loyal to my older Keychron K2, there are a few upgraded and newer versions to consider. Keychron has released a variety of new models over the past two years, with a broad range of features and price tags.

In many cases, the form factor is the draw. One of the more interesting releases, called the Keychron K8 HE Wireless Magnetic Switch Custom Keyboard, comes with an all-wood body and is equipped with an LED backlight. That one is substantially more expensive at around $200. The K2, meanwhile, costs $60. But if you’re into the look, maybe it’s worth it.

If you’re a gamer, there’s also Keychron’s C0 HE One-Handed 8K Keyboard , which is a keypad built for convenience and speed and has an industrial aesthetic to it. However, interested gamers will have to wait — as it’s currently sold out.

The company has also updated its K, Q, and V series keyboards, with many of those ranging in price from $100 to $200, depending on the features and model.

One of the appealing elements of owning a mechanical keyboard is the versatility. You can swap out the key caps for a wide variety of others (indeed, there’s a whole submarket devoted to this) or make your own custom caps (I’ve never gone that overboard).

There is also the sound, of course. Some people balk at the accentuated noise of loudly clacking keys, but I’m a fan. In fact, the sound is one of the key selling points for a lot of consumers. The distinct auditory experience produced by said keyboards has even made its way into ASMR videos .

For me, the Keychron’s biggest selling point is its retro form factor. I get really nostalgic for old school electronics, and Keychron scratches this itch pretty well. It’s a beautiful-looking device, which brings to mind a different era of computing, when the style was more workman-like, less minimalist.

As far as home office purchases go, you could do a lot worse than to pick yourself up a piece of hardware that makes your desk look like it just time-traveled from the 1990s.

articles.title: My brief romance with an AI bird feeder
articles.summary: Expensive AI-driven smart bird feeders can open your eyes to your local ecosystem. They can also attract pests.
articles.body: It started off promising enough. Dozens of tiny, colorful birds were drawn to my garden just a few weeks after I mounted a $350 $269 Kiwibit Bird Feeder 2 Pro. “Looks like Great Tit!” read the first AI-driven alert sent to my phone. “Looks like Eurasian Blue Tit!” read another. I chuckled, still waiting for adulthood to kick in. This went on for days. Hundreds of miniature tits came to snack on expensive sunflower seeds already husked. They’d skulk about in nearby trees before flittering in to grab a single seed to be safely enjoyed in the canopy above. [Image: I took great delight in my new house guests. I admired them in crisp 4K HDR video recordings. I looked for unique markings in the hope of naming my new feral pets. I clicked deeper into the Kiwibit app to read about my visitors’ migration habits, where they nest, and what they like to eat. It was all going swell until he arrived. “Looks like Common Wood Pigeon!” came the alert. All I saw was a battleship-gray blob obscuring the live camera feed. The winged rat was so fat and imposing that he blocked the lens. Ugh, no, go back to the tourists! In mild panic, I triggered the feeder’s Nuisance Animal Alarm, a feature typically reserved for squirrels and the like. The pigeon tensed, looked around, but wasn’t deterred by the audible siren that was surely annoying my neighbors. Soon it went back to gorging on the haute cuisine purchased for more refined guests. It ate and ate and ate. For 15 minutes, it ate until I walked outside and shooed it away. [Image: [Image: Thereafter, that pigeon, or pigeons (who can tell) moved in. They’d perch for 30 minutes or more, slamming their faces into the seed pile with the clumsy enthusiasm of a tween bobbing for apples. Mice arrived below to feast on the spoils. Admitting defeat, I dismounted the expensive bird feeder and shoved it into a closet. I’m not mad at Kiwibit. The “Bird Feeder 2 Pro 4K AI Camera with Solar Panel (Lifetime AI Included)” I tested was a joy to use, until it wasn’t. That’s not Kiwibit’s fault. [Image: You mad bro? If you’ve been tempted to buy a smart bird feeder, I’d suggest starting with something simple, inexpensive, and without AI instead of going all in on day one — you can’t return a used feeder just because it attracts pests.

articles.title: The leaked emails of 2007: What Steve Jobs and Eric Schmidt actually said when Google built Android
articles.summary: Long before Apple and Google became fierce rivals in the smartphone era, an exchange between Steve Jobs and Eric Schmidt revealed how seriously Silicon
articles.body: Long before Apple and Google became fierce rivals in the smartphone era, an exchange between Steve Jobs and Eric Schmidt revealed how seriously Silicon Valley leaders viewed the battle for engineering talent. According to a report by Reuters, court documents later made public lic showed jobs personally asked Google to stop recruiting Apple employees, prompting swift action from Google’s leadership. The emails that surfaced during the civil litigation involving Apple, Google and several other technology companies accused of conspiring to suppress employee compensation by limiting competition for skilled workers.A message from Apple founder Steve Jobs to ex-Google CEO Eric SchmidtAs reported by Reuters, when Jobs learned Google had targeted one of his employees, he emailed Schmidt directly, then Google's chairman, saying he "would be very pleased if your recruiting department would stop doing this." Schmidt forwarded the email to colleagues, writing that he believed Google had a policy of not recruiting from Apple and that this was a direct request from Jobs. The recruiting department replied that he should extend apologies as appropriate to Jobs, and the recruiter was fired.Google's senior staffing strategist told Schmidt the recruiter would be fired "within the hour." Schmidt called this an "appropriate response," and said he wanted HR to make a public example of the termination within the group and make it a strong part of new-hire training. Then came the smiley. After Schmidt told Jobs the recruiter would be fired, Jobs forwarded Schmidt's note to a top Apple human resources executive with a smiley face. Jobs did not reply to Schmidt with the smiley, as your headline implies. He sent it to his own HR chief.Eric Schmidt terminated at least two recruiters for violationsThe recruiter was not the only one. Judge Lucy Koh wrote that emails showed Schmidt "terminated at least two recruiters for violations of anti-solicitation agreements, and threatened to terminate more." She said Schmidt, Jobs and Intuit chairman Bill Campbell were "key players" in creating and enforcing the agreements.In another episode, Google sought to hire three former Apple engineers for a planned engineering center in Paris. Jobs wrote that Apple would "strongly prefer" that Google not hire them, and Google told him it had scrapped the plan "based on your strong preference."Other emails showed Jobs threatening rivals. Jobs told Palm's then-CEO Edward Colligan that if Palm kept targeting Apple employees, Apple would launch a patent lawsuit. Google co-founder Sergey Brin testified that Jobs had told him hiring one of Apple's people would mean "war," a reference to patent litigation. Shown the smiley email in his deposition, Brin reportedly said, "Wow, Steve used a smiley." Schmidt also seemed aware of the legal risk. When Google's HR director asked whether the no-recruiting policy could be shared with others, Schmidt said he preferred it be shared verbally because he did not want to create a paper trail he could be sued over later.ConsequencesThe lawsuit, filed in 2011 on behalf of more than 64,000 workers, alleged the agreements stopped employees from getting better job offers elsewhere. In 2014, Judge Koh rejected a proposed $324.5 million settlement, saying there was "substantial and compelling evidence" that Jobs was "a, if not the, central figure in the alleged conspiracy." The companies later agreed to a larger deal. The final figure was A$613.9 million, or roughly US$415 million.Schmidt later testified about Jobs' influence. "Steve was unhappy," he said, "and Steve's unhappiness absolutely influenced the change we made in recruiting practice."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: LG’s RGB LED TV is good for certain situations, but an OLED is better
articles.summary: A bunch of little issues add up to make the MRGB95B not worth the price when TVs from Sony, Samsung, Hisense, and TCL do it better.
articles.body: When it comes to TVs, the LG name has long been synonymous with OLEDs, continually leading Samsung and Sony as the top OLED manufacturer. But 2026 is all about RGB LED TVs. Almost every major company has released models with the new technology — including LG and its $3,600 75-inch Micro RGB evo MRGB95B that I’ve been testing. And while LG’s RGB LED TV benefits from the brightness and color capability the technology provides, it has issues I couldn’t overlook that its less expensive competitors don’t. The MRGB95B comes in three sizes, with the 75-inch being the smallest. It has four HDMI 2.1 ports, supports Dolby Vision — although not Dolby Vision 2 or HDR10+ — and comes with the Magic Remote design LG unveiled last year. It has a more traditional remote shape instead of the curved wand of previous versions. As with all LG TVs, the MRGB95B runs on webOS. It runs quickly, but I find it less intuitive to navigate than Google TV, Apple TV, or Roku. It supports all of the major streaming apps. [Product: LG MRGB95B RGB LED TV | Speaking of software, a quick note: LG has recently come under increased scrutiny after a video from Gamers Nexus showed security vulnerabilities and continuous audio recording on its TVs, which LG has denied. When setting up the MRGB95B, it’s only necessary to accept the terms of use and privacy policy if you want to use webOS. Otherwise, as with any TV, it can be disconnected from the internet, although an external streaming device would be needed for any streaming services (I use an Apple TV 4K, myself). OK, moving on. So, why buy an RGB LED TV? RGB LED TVs use zones of individual red, green, and blue LEDs as backlights as opposed to a field of white or blue LEDs that rely on a color filter or quantum dots to create the colors that reach our eyes. RGB LED TVs have a color filter, too, but since the backlight is already creating color based on what’s needed onscreen, the color filter doesn’t need to work as hard to dial that in. It allows for higher color brightness and the ability to display more colors. LG (and Samsung) use the term Micro RGB to describe the technology, while others say Mini RGB LED. And while the LG and Samsung RGBs are reportedly smaller (although neither has confirmed the exact size), it doesn’t directly translate into more zones or better performance over Mini RGB. [Image: [Image: As with all of the RGB LED TVs I’ve seen this year, the 95B gets very bright — I measured a peak of 4,011 nits in HDR Filmmaker mode — allowing it to deliver an impactful image even in a sunlit living room. And in a dark room, the highlights in scenes from The Meg really pop. At the other end of the spectrum, though, the LG struggles a bit. Near-black shadow detail, such as the corners of the living room and kitchen of Sapper Morton’s home at the beginning of Blade Runner 2049, is difficult to see. And when there are bright moments within a dark portion of the screen — subtitles are a good example — the LG exhibits more blooming than I’ve seen on other RGB LED TVs. --- LG MRGB95B specs Display type: RGB LED HDR formats: Dolby Vision, HDR10, HLG TV OS: webOS 26 HDMI inputs: 4 x HDMI 2.1 (one with eARC) Audio support: Dolby Atmos, Dolby Atmos FlexConnect, Dolby Digital, Auracast Gaming features: VRR, ALLM, Game Optimizer, G-Sync compatible Sizes available (inches): 75, 86, 100 --- The LG 95B can display really vibrant colors thanks to the RGB LED technology. It’s able to cover 100 percent of the P3 color gamut (which is what’s used for films) and nearly 90 percent of the larger BT.2020 color area. But even in Filmmaker mode out of the box, those colors still show visible accuracy issues. Overall, the TV leans toward light blue, so white clouds have a slight blue tint to them and skin tones are cooler than they should be. After a few days living with the LG MRGB95B, I got used to the slightly blue image (although it was still noticeable). A $3,600 TV in 2026 shouldn’t have the inaccuracies on the MRGB95B. While the TV performs well in a bright room during the day, when the sun goes down and the lamps turn on, they can wreak havoc on the image. The 95B’s glossy coating is one of the most reflective I’ve seen in a long time. In moderately lit rooms, a lamp or ceiling light directly reflected on the screen causes rainbows to dance across the image. It’s not as bad when the scene is bright, such as the scorching desert of Arrakis in Dune, but once we enter the dark corridors of House Harkonnen, the reflections become incredibly noticeable. Viewing angles are always a problem for LED TVs — RGB or not — and that’s evident on the LG, too. When only moderately off-axis, the colors become washed out, losing their vibrancy for anyone who’s sitting off to the side. [Image: [Image: In a vacuum, the MRGB95B is a good TV for certain situations. It’s really bright and stands up to ambient light well (just avoid having ceiling, wall, or standing lights reflected on the screen), and the colors are vibrant if not totally accurate out of the box. But it doesn’t hold up against other TVs. The Sony Bravia 7 II (which you can find $1,300 cheaper at 75 inches) has better color accuracy and handles reflections better. And the Hisense UR9 performs comparably for less money, too. But the real competition comes from within LG itself. The LG G6 OLED is only a few hundred dollars more than the MRGB95B, as is the Samsung S95H, and both of those TVs offer significantly better performance with superior color accuracy and viewing angles. The OLEDs don’t get quite as bright, but since they can turn off light at the pixel level, contrast is remarkable and there’s zero blooming. LG has always struggled to make competitive LED TVs, and that trend continues with the MRGB95B. In fact, it might be LG’s best argument to get an LG OLED TV. Photography by John Higgins / The Verge --- How I test TVs I set up each TV in my living room on my home theater credenza. I stream movies and shows through the TV’s apps and from an Apple TV 4K, play discs on my Oppo UDP-203 4K Blu-ray player (including the Spears & Munsil Ultra HD Benchmark disc), and play games on my Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5. This is done at different times of the day and under different lighting conditions, with curtains open, with lamps and overhead lights on, or with blackout curtains up to keep the room dark. While I am a certified ISF Level 3 calibrator, I do not calibrate the TVs before measurement, as the overwhelming majority of TV owners don’t bother. So it’s important to know how well the TVs perform out of the box, with minor tweaks in the menu anyone can do. For measurement, I use Portrait Displays’ Calman color calibration software, a Murideo 8K Seven pattern generator, an X-rite i1 Pro 3 spectrophotometer, Portrait Displays’ C6 HDR5000 colorimeter, a Konica Minolta LS-100 luminance meter, and Leo Bodnar 4K lag tester.

articles.title: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US
articles.summary: Roofs were ripped off buildings after Isaias barrelled into the US on Friday evening, before it weakened to a post-tropical cyclone.
articles.body:
Four people have died and hundreds of thousands are without power after Hurricane Isaias battered parts of the southern US with powerful winds and heavy rain.

Officials reported two deaths each in the states of Alabama and Florida, which included people who were killed when trees fell on their houses.

At least 500,000 people were without power in several states as of Saturday evening, according to tracker PowerOutage.

Isaias made landfall in Florida late on Friday with maximum sustained winds of 105mph (168km/h) before being downgraded to a post-tropical cyclone.

The storm felled trees and ripped the roofs off buildings. Alabama, Florida and Georgia all declared states of emergency ahead of its arrival, while both Florida and Alabama issued mandatory evacuation orders to thousands of people.

Meanwhile, Hurricane Simon is bearing down on Mexico's Pacific coast and has strengthened to category four. It is expected to make landfall sometime overnight.

Tropical Storm Rachel, also in the Pacific Ocean, is expected to hit southern California later on Saturday.

Two deaths related to Isaias were reported in Florida's Escambia County. A woman was killed when a tree fell on her house, local Sheriff Chip Simmons said.

Joey Williams told NewsNation his wife had died in the storm. He said they went outside to snap pictures of the damage but, when they went back into their home, a tree fell through the roof and trapped them.

"I was able to squeeze out. My wife didn't make it," Williams told the outlet.

Simmons later reported that a man had died from carbon monoxide poisoning after running a generator in a garage that was not properly ventilated. Four other people who were in the same house were taken to hospital.

Officials had to rescue people in vehicles that became submerged by floodwaters. The Florida National Guard shared pictures of a truck stuck in a flood ditch, saying soldiers "stopped, swam to the vehicle and pulled its occupants to safety".

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said flooding was a continued risk and warned of a "very hazardous situation".

In neighbouring Alabama, a sheriff was injured when a tree fell on him as he was responding to a car crash.

"Unfortunately, we have also learned that two Alabamians have lost their lives," Governor Kay Ivey said in a post on X, without giving further details on the circumstances of the deaths.

She also said officials were concerned about "spinoff tornadoes" in the state from the strong winds and heavy rain.

"As we approach the weekend and any travel plans, make sure you have reliable information as conditions develop," she said.

In Charleston, South Carolina, officials asked people to stay home on Saturday night as high tide is expected to reach 7.5ft (2.3m).

"After dark, floodwater is much harder to see and it's impossible to judge how deep it is from behind the wheel," the city said.

The storm is expected to continue to weaken as it travels to the north-east, but the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) warned that the Carolinas and Georgia could see floods from up to 10 inches (25cm) of rainfall.

Hurricane Isaias was the first hurricane in the Atlantic's hurricane season, which largely has been delayed due to El Niño conditions in the Pacific.

articles.title: Chevrolet deixa S10 mais bruta para o off-road na versão Trail Boss. | G1
articles.standfirst: Versão de R$ 341 mil ganhou suspensão elevada em 30 mm, pneus para terra e lama e visual exclusivo, mantendo motor turbodiesel de 207 cv. O g1 testou a picape para descobrir se as mudanças comprometem o conforto no asfalto.
articles.summary: Picape tem suspensão elevada, pneus para uso no fora de estrada e visual exclusivo. Motor 2.8 turbo diesel, câmbio automático de 8 marchas e tração 4x4 completam a receita.
articles.body:
Chevrolet S10 Trail Boss 2027 — Foto: Divulgação / GM

A Chevrolet lançou a nova versão Trail Boss com o argumento de que ela foi preparada e afinada para encarar trilhas. Esta S10 tem uma suspensão mais alta e mais forte para poder voltar ilesa de uma aventura.

Pode parecer irônico que uma montadora precise criar uma versão ainda mais raiz e bruta de uma picape que, em essência, já nasceu pronta para esse tipo de desafio. Mas outras marcas já fizeram isso, então a estratégia não chega a ser novidade.

É verdade que, com o passar dos anos, as picapes médias foram incorporando elementos e acertos que as deixaram muito mais amigáveis ao asfalto.

Toyota Hilux, Ford Ranger, Volkswagen Amarok, Nissan Frontier, Mitsubishi L200 Triton e a própria S10 passam a maior parte do tempo na estrada, e os acertos ajudam a vender mais.

Vendas das picapes médias entre janeiro e agosto de 2026:

Basta analisar o perfil dessas picapes. Elas têm cada vez mais tecnologia e eletrônica. O acabamento interno incorpora elementos refinados, que oferecem muito mais uma experiência de luxo do que a robustez necessária para enfrentar o barro.

O g1 levou a S10 Trail Boss para a cidade, onde a picape deve passar a maior parte do tempo e também enfrentar obstáculos, como valetas, buracos e restos de obras inacabadas.

O objetivo é entender se as mudanças feitas pela Chevrolet na S10 reforçaram o DNA aventureiro da picape sem abrir mão do conforto e do luxo esperados de um veículo que custa R$ 341.290 .

A Chevrolet fez várias mudanças no visual da picape, mas as mais importantes estão escondidas sob a carroceria.

O modelo foi desenvolvido em parceria com a divisão de performance da General Motors e sai de fábrica com suspensão elevada, pneus específicos e pacote visual exclusivo, mantendo os padrões de segurança e a garantia original da marca.

O conjunto de suspensão, assinado pela Ironman , é o principal diferencial da picape. O kit traz mola e amortecedor recalibrados em conjunto com a geometria da picape, elevando a parte dianteira em cerca de 30 mm.

🔎 A Ironman 4x4 foi fundada em 1958 na Austrália por Guenter Jacob, um imigrante alemão e engenheiro. Hoje, a Ironman 4x4 é uma marca global que fornece produtos de suspensão e acessórios de alta resistência para aventuras.

Com a mudança, o modelo passa a ter vão livre do solo de 324 mm, ângulo de ataque de 32,5° e ângulo de saída de 22,9°. Esses números são importantes, pois mostram que a Trail Boss não vai raspar a dianteira e traseira. Nem bater o fundo em obstáculos.

Os amortecedores da Ironman foram codesenvolvidos com a GM e validados em laboratórios, passando por 26 ensaios com padrão global de corrosão da empresa.

A modificação na altura exigiu a recalibração dos módulos eletrônicos, dos sensores e da câmera frontal. Com isso, sistemas como alerta de colisão com frenagem automática de emergência, assistente de permanência em faixa e controle eletrônico de estabilidade foram revalidados para o novo acerto.

A picape é equipada com pneus Pirelli Scorpion All-Terrain de 18 polegadas, projetados para entregar tração em terra, cascalho e lama, além de manter o comportamento no asfalto.

Visualmente, a S10 Trail Boss conta com:

Grade dianteira com a gravata "Black Bowtie" em preto brilhante;

Rodas escurecidas com desenho exclusivo;

Estribo tubular integrado ao santantônio estendido.

O modelo também traz adesivos exclusivos, a palavra Chevrolet em relevo na caçamba e emblemas da Ironman.

No interior, o veículo apresenta acabamento escurecido , bancos com tecido central aveludado e o nome da versão bordado nos encostos de cabeça. O painel inclui quadro de instrumentos digital de 8 polegadas e central multimídia MyLink de 11 polegadas.

A lista de conectividade traz o sistema OnStar com Wi-Fi nativo, atualização remota de sistemas e aplicativo para comandos à distância, como travamento de portas e partida remota.

O modelo oferece entradas USB dos tipos A e C, carregador por indução e integração Android Auto compatível com o Gemini, do Google.

A caçamba vem equipada de série com o protetor Multiflex e santantônio estendido, que servem de apoio para acessórios originais, como bandejas organizadoras, divisórias e suportes para o transporte de equipamentos.

Chevrolet S10 Trail Boss 2027. — Foto: Divulgação / GM

O conjunto mecânico utiliza o motor Duramax 2.8 turbodiesel de 207 cv e 52 kgfm de torque , combinado ao câmbio automático de oito marchas e tração 4x4 com reduzida acionada por comando rotativo. A calibração foi adaptada ao biodiesel brasileiro.

De acordo com dados do Inmetro, a picape registra consumo de 8,3 km/l na cidade e 10,5 km/l na estrada.

6 airbags (frontais, laterais e de cortina);

Parece algo estranho uma montadora lançar uma versão ainda mais parruda de um veículo que nasceu off-road. Mas não é incomum isso acontecer. A própria Toyota já fez isso com a Hilux GR Gazoo Racing.

Na S10 Trail Boss, as mudanças estão essencialmente na suspensão. A maior altura na dianteira e todo o novo conjunto deixam a picape ainda mais preparada para encarar o fora de estrada.

Isso atende ao desejo de clientes que exploram o interior do Brasil e não querem ficar pelo caminho.

Para dar visibilidade às mudanças e ao caráter especial da versão, há também alterações estéticas. O resultado fica a critério de cada um. Gosto e design, claro, são particulares .

Cabine da Chevrolet S10 Trail Boss 2027. — Foto: Divulgação / GM

O g1 testou a S10 na cidade de São Paulo, em algumas vias apertadas, um desafio que a picape pode enfrentar no uso cotidiano.

Também foi possível encarar uma espécie de off-road urbano, com valetas, buracos e obras inacabadas espalhadas pela capital paulista, sem problemas.

Nos poucos trechos em altas velocidades, os pneus, feitos para encarar o barro, não mostraram tanto ruído dentro da cabine. Para quem leva uma S10 mais preparada para aventuras, porém, já é esperado um comportamento mais rústico.

O interessante é que a picape recebeu essas mudanças e parece ter se adaptado bem a elas. Isso se reflete nos testes realizados pela GM para aplicar a nova suspensão e os pneus.

Para quem vê alguns carros modificados, pode parecer que basta colocar uma suspensão diferente para, em questão de dias, a picape estar pronta. Para uma montadora, é necessário validar esse conjunto.

É diferente, por exemplo, de uma modificação de suspensão essencialmente visual, como o g1 já mostrou na picape da cantora Ana Castela .

A conclusão é que a S10, apesar do nome forte, se prepara para uma concorrência cada vez maior . A Ranger cresce em vendas e já se estabeleceu como a picape mais amigável de dirigir em seu segmento, com um comportamento que vai quase na direção de um SUV. A S10 tem uma proposta mais raiz.

A Hilux vai receber uma atualização em breve, então ainda será necessário ver como ela chegará, já que é a líder de vendas.

O g1 já mostrou que a Volkswagen prepara uma nova Amarok que, pela tecnologia e pelo posicionamento, deve ter outro apelo. Um cliente mais interessado em ostentar uma picape do futuro do que mostrar uma picape para chafurdar a lama.

O mercado de picapes no Brasil é gigante. A disputa não se limita às grandes. Começa desde modelos menores, como a BYD Mako , a Volkswagen Tukan e, mais recentemente, a Renault Niagara. Isso sem esquecer de Fiat Strada e Toro, e também Chevrolet Montana e os modelos da RAM.

A Trail Boss segue a receita tradicional de quem gosta de picape à moda antiga , mas com um tempero ainda mais off-road, justamente para lembrar as origens de quem curte trilhas e estradas de terra.

Ela é perfeita para o cliente que acredita que as picapes estão perdendo espírito de aventura. Gosta de uma picape com pegada mais delicada? A Trail Boss não para você.

articles.title: Nicolas Cage says he won't work with Amazon again over AI dispute
articles.summary: Nicolas Cage, who recently starred in "Spider-Noir," said he won't work with Amazon again after a disagreement over an AI waiver.
articles.body:
Nicolas Cage is making it clear — he's not an "AI-friendly actor."

The 62-year-old actor spoke out against a tech giant during an appearance at New York Comic Con on Saturday. He alleged that he was asked to sign an artificial intelligence waiver for the television series "Spider Noir."

" Amazon is a very AI-friendly company, to the tune of $50 billion invested in OpenAI," Cage said on stage.

"I am not an AI-friendly actor, so it's like, connect those dots! I'm not a member of their club. I didn't sign the waiver to let him use AI on 'Spider-Noir.' I'm probably not going to be working with that studio again, but that's OK."

Amazon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The use of AI continues to be a major sticking point across Hollywood. Industry unions including SAG-AFTRA and the Writers Guild recently secured protections against technology in new contracts. But as AI evolves and AI actors like Tilly Norwood continue to make headlines, it's still unclear exactly how the industry will be affected.

"Spider-Noir," which premiered in May, is a "Spider-Man" project that put a 1930s crime-thriller spin on the web-slinging superhero. The show was produced by both Sony Pictures Television and Amazon MGM Studios.

Cage's part as "The Spider" marked his first leading role in a series. The Oscar-winning actor, whose home in Malibu was recently affected by a sinkhole , is known best for his roles in movies like "National Treasure," "Moonstruck" and "The Rock."

Upon its release, "Spider-Noir" received much praise from fans and critics alike. In its first six weeks of streaming, the series earned 2.6 billion minutes watched, according to Nielsen. It was also Amazon's most-nominated show at this year's Emmys , with 11 nominations and five wins.

Last month, Amazon announced that the show was canceled after only one season, leaving much of the industry in shock.

During his Comic Con panel, Cage also said he plans to keep working in TV. He announced that he will be joining the HBO series "True Detective."

"My agent's out there somewhere listening," Cage said. "That's OK that I'm the first to announce that, right?"

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: “Saturday Night Live” recap: Shane Gillis drops F-bomb in Dr. Seuss sketch, sending show into chaos
articles.summary: The former ‘SNL’ cast member returned to host for a third time, this time with Rosalía as musical guest.
articles.body:
Hey all — it's SNL in Review with our rubber match for the start of season 52. The consensus from the peanut gallery on the past two episodes seems to be focused on weak writing. Which is a problem when you consider the sheer number of people on the writing staff. No one wants to admit it, but there's something fundamentally off about the modern show. As Alan Sepinwall put it this week, SNL frequently is "at sea when it comes to dealing with political turmoil" in the current Trump 2.0 environment.

Tonight's show will be an interesting test case to that point: it is the return of Shane Gillis . We do not need to relitigate the controversy beyond to say, this is his third time hosting . As Lorne himself put it to Steve Martin in his recent doc: Gillis is easily one of the most significant and successful stand-up comedians working today. (His thrice gigs as host + Lorne's POV make me wonder if the members of the fanbase that clutched pearls so, so tightly about his hiring feel silly now? Or no.)

I guess tonight is about threes: third episode of the season, third hosting stint by Gillis. And third appearance overall tonight by musical guest Rosalía. She first appeared on SNL as a guest performer alongside Bad Bunny in 2021, then returned a year later as the featured musical guest when Zoë Kravitz hosted.

USS Lincoln has been gone for over 300 days. Before the brave men and women get to return to their families, they will be hearing from one person: ah yes, Colin Jost 's Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. It's been seven months of war, and they're greeted by a bombastic man wearing mini liquor bottles as a belt, who updates them on what has been happening domestically.

He runs through some headlines. "Public executions are back! Kinda like Scrubs !" He has a new logo — it's an American eagle "with a Nazi vibe."

Next: Hegseth introduces RFK Jr. (James Austin Johnson). The impression is… solid, leading to a funny punchline wherein Hegseth smacks him on the back, and his voice immaculately returns to normal. I just can't get into Jost's delivery — having him croon Linkin Park was never on my bingo card. What are we doing here?

Former cast member Victoria Jackson offers: "Colin is a good Hegseth. RFK impression is funny, but he should've had a deep tan. I wish they would skewer the left as mercilessly as they always skewer the right."

Shane is "fine," he claims; he has a couple things he's dealing with, like losing weight. He notes he was in a Bud Light commercial this year, and thinks he looked "like a lesbian" seeing himself onscreen.

He discusses going on hikes solo and checking out public gyms in New York. He discusses women's shorts and kettlebells. His "friend, Joe Rogan" has a sauna in his Texas podcast studio, and mentions Theo Von insulting him (by calling him a "wet egg"). Gillis segues into his sisters raising him, and the psychological impact of their insults. Ouch! "And that was the monologue!" he ends.

Former cast member Jeff Richards comments that Gillis is a clearly "really funny guy, obvious natural. I have been touring with William Montgomery and think he'd be an excellent host. It's great seeing guys like him, Shane, Kam Patterson get exposure. When people aren't streaming Pay To Die , I recommend watching Tires and Busboys !"

Victoria Jackson, for her part, says the monologue is "good. Shane looks skinny/handsome! He's right about gym girls dressing like 'whores.' When did 'camel toe' become acceptable gym fashion and grocery shopping attire? Did Molly Shannon's Sally O'Malley make it cool?"

It's the only talk show by police officers, for everyone. Law enforcement wants to show it's not scary talking to cops. Shane Gillis is the host, and he interrogates his first guest Lawrence Kornfeld (Jeremy Culhane), who is promoting his book. Gillis and his partner/sidekick are very suspicious and hostile to him, like on a traffic stop — he even has a window on the couch to roll down. Next: Ben Marshall gets tased. "Big time scumbag!"

Fun moment: Kam Patterson comes out as a comedian who is performing at Magoobys. (Fun fact: I saw Kam perform at Magoobys outside Baltimore earlier this year.) Kam takes one look at the white cops and immediately leaves the set. Victoria Jackson calls this one "accurate."

Very active audience so far. I could hear boisterous reception to certain cast members during the opening credits.

Tommy Brennan, Andrew Dismukes, and James Austin Johnson play a country western band serenading a wedding, during a couple's first dance. It's actually a tribute/inner monologue for the father of the bride. He's busy reflecting on raising a girl who is now a young woman, which means, well — now her childhood bedroom is his! Her stuff is packed up, and he has a lot of creative ideas of what he will do. Popcorn machine? Video games and pinball?!

It's 1920 in Lowell, Massachusetts. Fillmore Footwear has invented a new shoe design. Typically, shoes are leather and loud. But now they're lighter and more flexible. They're good for running… walking… and — as Shane Gillis notes — sneaking… yes, it is a "Sneaker".

Other executives find that term creepy, indeed Gillis has a dark line of thinking... "I've always wondered why Sneakers were called sneakers! Runwell's was clever, historical, and educational! Good ending," says Victoria Jackson.

Curse word alert! Shane Gillis drops an obvious F-bomb, as a son irate that his dad (Mikey Day) is being asked repeatedly whether he wants a breakfast order he's clearly declined, multiple times. Lots of Dr. Seuss references here obviously. it starts with the Sam I Am premise with Andrew Dismukes, and gets broadened to Sarah Sherman in a really fun cameo.

Day saves the day with an adlib, mentioning the "bad word!" I was disappointed Shane Gillis didn't have a fun quip in the moment to recover. But Day did it! He's going big this season for sure, very present.

For the record: Day and Kristen Wiig played a married Who couple forced into an uncomfortable Christmas-morning conversation with their children after a sleazy, bisexual Grinch (Pete Davidson) crashes in their bed, following a raucous holiday party. Day later took on the role of the Grinch himself in Love Is Blind: Grinch Edition , a surreal parody of the Netflix dating series in which Ariana Grande's contestant discovers her mystery pod match is the green holiday icon.

"This whole process is going to be a nightmare," promises Shane Gillis' spokesman. After a pleasant demo, the real workers will show up to upgrade a home's HVAC system… and it will be a disaster. They will save you money, but it will cost you! Fun, little long.

Victoria Jackson calls this one "GREAT. I recently had a similar experience; a near finger amputation of the repair man, my mailbox knocked down by his truck, and I stepped on a board he left in the grass that had 2 nails sticking straight up that went through my sandal into my foot. I got a tetanus shot and went on antibiotics."

This has a heavy ballet influence, even incorporating pointe shoes! Very powerful and beautiful. Probably the best musical performance of the season to date.

Victoria Jackson notes, "Rosalia is singing in Spanish, I can't understand the words. But, I like her tutu a lot. Actually, I can never understand the lyrics of the musical hosts. They mumble. Hey, maybe I'm deaf!"

Topics this week include President Trump losing the Nobel Peace Prize and the new War Department logo. National No Bra Day gets a Che quip.

Our first commentator tonight is Kevin O'Leary, a.k.a. Mr. Shark Tank 's Mr. Wonderful, who comes on to discuss massive data centers. James Austin Johnson portrayed O'Leary earlier this season, he's incredible. He's building a big data center, with a very evil name, in Utah. Noise and water issues, no matter. This is brilliant, one of my favorite segments of the year.

For some fall family fun, we get tips from a mom whose babysitter just cancelled. Ashley Padilla plays the mom, and her daughter, Coco, is played by Grace Reiter . The crowd gives them a big welcome. "I love you," justifies Padilla's mom after shrieking at her child. "My mom kissed a farm," blurts out Coco, who recounts getting lost in a corn maze. Coco just wants to know who her dad is!

Grace Reiter is playing an elderly woman on her final days. Hospice nurse Sarah Sherman suggests her son, Fred (Shane Gillis), stick around for the weekend in case she passes. He pauses: could this wait until Monday? He has tickets to see Jelly Roll at the Sphere.

Jelly Roll's spirit appears to Fred, and tells him to come to the show. Solid character work by Ben Marshall as Jelly! Cool Jesus also gives his approval. A few other visitors appear to him, including Rosalía… and his dead mom! Nice to see Reiter get a few at-bats tonight. "With Teddy Swims!" And a fun hook: Fred will be joining his mom in heaven soon anyway!

Victoria Jackson's verdict: this was "funny and smart." I agree.

A rainy, moving performance. Easily strongest guest so far this season.

"Clayton Middle School Chess Semifinals"

It's Tommy Brennan versus Jeremy Culhane in a quiet chess tournament. Culhane's character is mortified as his parents have come to cheer him on, and they are white trash and loud. Grace Reiter again gets the call, opposite Shane Gillis as her ex. And we get a Stapleview reunion, with Jane Wickline as Gillis' current, embarrassed girlfriend. Reiter and Gillis reunite, full of passion, and completely disrupt the chess match. Intense! Can't overstate the importance of this show for Grace.

OK, time for a break! Vote ! See everyone on Halloween!

I am still thinking about the F-bomb tonight! Notable examples include Charles Rocket's on-air F-bomb in 1981, Jenny Slate accidentally swearing during her first episode in 2009, and Kristen Stewart dropping an uncensored F-bomb during her 2017 monologue.

The show also weirdly has a close association with Dr. Seuss and playing the Cat in the Hat specifically. Hello, Mike Myers. Hello, Bill Hader.

Thanks again to Jeff Richards. Speaking of Halloween, check out his slasher spoof, Pay To Die , now on Tubi!

Thank you, Victoria Jackson! She concludes: "Very strong, talented cast this year. Although I wish Update's Michael Che would enunciate. He speaks with his mouth closed and I can't hear the words so I can't get the joke. Maybe I'm deaf."

"Sorry about earlier," Shane says in the goodnights. Was this the best episode of the season to date? Good use of Tommy Brennan, Kam Patterson… and Grace Reiter!

articles.title: What to expect from Apple’s ‘Welcome Home’ event
articles.summary: Get ready for a smart home hub, a refreshed HomePod Mini, a faster Apple TV, and maybe some LG smart locks.
articles.body: We are quickly coming up on Apple’s “Welcome Home” launch event, where we expect a host of smart home-related announcements. We are expecting refreshes to Apple TV and HomePod Mini, as well as a brand new smart home hub. We could also see the debut of a new platform called homeOS, and some partner devices from LG. What we probably won’t be seeing is the long-rumored touchscreen MacBook, which Cupertino whisperer Mark Gurman says will debut later this month. “Welcome Home” will officially kick off in New York on October 13th at 9AM ET. Here’s more about what to expect. A proper smart home hub Until now, Apple has primarily relied on the Home app to control all the various bits and bobs that make up your smart home. But it’s a market niche that the company has been eager to tackle more fully. The new device, which could be called HomePad or HomeView or, more simply, Apple Home Hub, will reportedly feature a 6-inch square touchscreen that can either be mounted on a wall or placed on a table or countertop. According to Mark Gurman, the countertop model will somewhat resemble the iMac G4, with the screen attached to an arm set into a half sphere. Gurman seems to believe the device will be called HomeView, rather than HomePad. In part he believes that decision was driven by the fact that the hub will not be an iPad-like experience since there will be no App Store. It will also supposedly use voice or facial recognition to identify who is interacting with it, pulling up the relevant contacts, calendar appointments, and more. Apple will offer the option for secondary identification through an iPhone to keep personal data more secure. The whole thing will reportedly run a new software platform called… homeOS The company may have registered a trademark for the name through a shell company called Home Operations Suite LLC, a move that Apple has pulled before to quietly secure the rights to names. The platform will supposedly feature a streamlined interface that “looks like a mashup of iOS, tvOS and watchOS,” according to Gurman. The focus, obviously, will be on smart home applications, like controlling thermostats and smart locks, and it will also be capable of making FaceTime calls. The OS will also include your usual assortment of Apple apps and widgets, including Apple Music, Podcasts, and News, as well as Reminders, Notes, and Siri AI. HomePod Mini and Apple TV get a minor refresh Word is that not much is changing with the HomePod Mini or Apple TV. The designs will remain the same, but they’ll get a new processor to help handle the added demand of Siri AI. This will be the first update to the HomePod Mini since it was announced on October 13th of 2020 — exactly six years before Apple’s Welcome Home event. While the company isn’t making any dramatic changes for the Mini’s birthday, it will be offering it in new colors, including green and pink. This will be the first hardware refresh for the Apple TV since 2022. In addition to supporting Siri AI, the new processor will also speed up navigation, which can get a bit laggy. Rumors are that it will have an integrated mic so that you won’t need to talk into the remote or a paired HomePod to control the Apple TV with Siri. The remote will also apparenlty have a speaker to make it easier to find. Both are expected to feature Apple’s N1 chip, which includes support for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 6.0. LG and other partner devices [Media: It’s likely that we’ll get a mention of products that integrate with HomeKit and offer new features built on top of homeOS and whatever Apple’s hardware hub ends up being called. But don’t expect Apple to share too much of the spotlight with its partners. We’ve already seen a leak of LG smart home, including deadbolts, thermostats, and more. They’ll also reportedly include an NFC-based “Proximity Control” that pops up a hint in the iPhone’s Dynamic Island when held near the device, as well as a “tap to set up without power” pairing feature. Update October 11th, 2026: Added additional rumors from Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter.

articles.title: Your phone can fix badly framed photos after you take them
articles.summary: Apple Intelligence in iOS 27 adds Extend and Reframe tools to Photos, letting iPhones generate new background areas beyond your original borders.
articles.body: Have you ever taken a photo you really liked, only to realize later that you stood too close, cut off part of the background or framed the subject in the wrong spot? Normally, fixing that means cropping even more of the photo. Now your phone may be able to go in the other direction. Apple added new Extend and Reframe tools to Photos in iOS 27. Instead of simply cutting away part of an image, Apple Intelligence can generate additional areas around the original shot or change its perspective after you take it. Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel phones offer similar AI editing tools that can help rescue photos that did not come out quite the way you planned. Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better health care . Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist . See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com 12 BIGGEST APPLE WWDC 2026 TAKEAWAYS YOU NEED TO KNOW What is new for photos in iOS 27? Apple added several Apple Intelligence upgrades to Photos with iOS 27. Two of the most useful are Extend and Reframe. Extend lets you expand a photo beyond its original borders. For example, if someone's head is too close to the top of the image or you want more space around the subject, Apple Intelligence can generate additional background. Reframe goes further. Apple says it lets you change the point of capture after taking the photo. You can move the image, zoom, rotate it and adjust its perspective while Apple Intelligence generates the additional portions needed for the new composition. These tools go beyond traditional cropping. Cropping removes part of your image. Extend and Reframe can create parts of the image that were never captured by the camera. Because these are generative AI features, take a close look at the final result. AI-generated areas can sometimes contain strange details, especially around faces, hands, text or complicated backgrounds. Which iPhones can use Extend and Reframe? Extend and Reframe require Apple Intelligence and iOS 27 or later. Apple Intelligence works on: Availability can also depend on your language and region. Apple says some Apple Intelligence features may have usage limits. If you have an older iPhone that can install iOS 27 but does not support Apple Intelligence, you will not get these particular editing tools. How to extend a photo on iPhone in iOS 27 Use Extend when you want more room around the subject or need to expand the edges of your original photo. If you change your mind later, Apple lets you return to the editing tools and reset the Extend changes. CALIFORNIA LAW PUTS DIGITAL FINGERPRINTS ON AI FAKES How to reframe a photo on iPhone in iOS 27 Use Reframe when the composition or perspective feels wrong rather than simply too tight. This can be especially useful when your subject is awkwardly positioned or you wish you had held the camera at a slightly different angle. How to fix a badly framed photo on a Samsung Galaxy Samsung takes a somewhat different approach. Compatible Galaxy phones use Galaxy AI Photo Assist, which includes tools for moving, removing and adding objects in a photo. For this trick, the Move tool is the one to use. It lets you reposition, rotate or resize part of the image, then uses generative AI to fill in the background created by your changes. Samsung's standard Gallery editor also lets you change the aspect ratio, rotate the picture and adjust its angle. How to use Photo Assist on a compatible Samsung Galaxy Menus can vary slightly by Galaxy model and software version. 8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT How to fix a badly framed photo on Google Pixel Google Photos has one of the closest Android alternatives to Apple's new Extend tool. It's called Auto frame. Google says Auto frame can recompose a photo that is too tightly cropped or poorly framed. It can also use AI to fill in missing areas and extend the background. How to use Auto frame on Google Pixel Make sure you have the latest version of the Google Photos app. Google also includes Straighten, Rotate, Perspective and Aspect ratio controls in the same Crop section if you want to make the adjustment yourself. Google rolls out some Photos features gradually. Therefore, if you do not see Auto frame, update Google Photos and check again. Availability can also vary by device, account and region. 5 tips for getting better results with AI photo editing AI photo editing works best when you give it a reasonably clear original image. Here are a few things to keep in mind. 1) Start with a sharp photo AI can generate new areas around an image, but it cannot completely rescue every blurry or badly exposed shot. Start with the clearest version you have. 2) Make smaller changes first Instead of dramatically expanding the entire picture, try adding a little extra space around the edges. Smaller edits can look more natural. 3) Look closely at people Zoom in before saving. Check faces, hands, hair, jewelry and clothing for unexpected changes. 4) Check signs and other text Generative AI can struggle with letters and numbers. Look closely at street signs, shirts, storefronts and anything else containing text. 5) Keep the original When your phone gives you the option, save the edited version as a copy. That way, you still have the untouched photo if the AI result does not look right later. Kurt's key takeaways One of the frustrating things about smartphone photography is realizing you almost got the perfect shot. Maybe you stood a little too close, left the person too far to one side or tilted the camera just enough to make the composition feel wrong. iOS 27 gives supported iPhones another way to fix those mistakes with Extend and Reframe. I also like that Galaxy and Pixel owners have comparable options instead of sitting this one out. These tools will not replace taking a well-framed photo in the first place, but they can give a photo you would otherwise delete another shot. articles.title: Nine desk gadgets that can make your workday better
articles.summary: The right desk gadgets can help you reduce clutter, stay focused, and add a little extra convenience to your day.
articles.body:
We spend dozens of hours at our desks each week, if not more, so it’s worth creating a workspace that’s productive and enjoyable. The right desk gadgets can help reduce clutter, stay focused, and add a little extra convenience to the day.

From ambient lighting to smart mugs, there are lots of products designed to make the time you spend at your own desk better, so we’ve combined a list of some options that we’ve tried and liked. Whether you’re working from home or in an office, these gadgets are worth checking out if you’re looking to transform your workspace.

Mount-It! Under Desk Cable Management Tray — $40

If your desk is cluttered with cords or a giant surge protector, Mount-It!’ s cable management tray is a great option. It mounts under your desk without drilling or screws, and it keeps cables and power strips off the floor and out of sight while still within reach when you need to plug something in. It holds up to 11 pounds, surprisingly, and fits desktops from 0.2″ to 1.97″ thick.

The tray is available on Amazon for $39.99.

It’s currently on sale on Amazon for $12.99. Who couldn’t use three drawers for essentials like stamps and perhaps a harmless little candy bar to get you through the afternoon?

The Anker Nano Charging Station combines plugs, USB-C, and USB-A ports with retractable charging cables into a single compact charger. The station has a 1.3-inch LCD screen that displays real-time power output and temperature.

You can charge a laptop, phone, tablet, earbuds, and other devices on the same station, getting off the need for multiple chargers around your workspace. The retractable cables make it easy to plug in a device when needed without cluttering up your desk with extra wires. (We love a retractable cable!)

Logitech Lift Vertical Ergonomic Wireless Mouse — $80

If you’re working at your desk all day, a standard mouse can be hard on your wrist. The Logitech Lift Vertical Mouse is designed to promote a more natural posture in the forearm. It’s a good fit for small to medium hands, and there’s also a left-handed option available.

The vertical mouse has six customizable buttons that offer quick access to shortcuts, and connects wirelessly via Bluetooth or with the included USB receiver.

The Odistar desktop vacuum is an affordable option for keeping your desk clean and crumb-free, especially if you eat meals at your desk (hey, sometimes it’s unavoidable). You can also use it to clean your keyboard and remove dust and debris between keys.

It’s quiet and simple to use, and because it’s so compact, you can keep it on your desk or tuck it away in a drawer until you need it. It’s cordless and uses two AA batteries. At just $9.99 as part of Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days , the desktop vacuum is a great way to keep your desk clean as you work.

If you’re someone who enjoys hot coffee but often finds yourself drinking it cold after getting sidetracked while working, the Ember Mug 2 can help keep your drinks at the perfect temperature.

You can set an exact temperature using your phone and the smart mug maintains it for up to one and a half hours with the 10-ounce version and up to 80 minutes with the 12-ounce version. The mug allows for a more consistent coffee experience, making your workday more enjoyable.

The Amazon Echo Dot can be a great addition to your work desk as you can use voice commands to set reminders, create to-do lists, check your calendar, play music, adjust smart lights, or get quick answers to questions without having to reach for your phone.

Because it’s small, you can easily place it anywhere on your desk where it can act as a hands-free assistant that helps keep you organized and focused throughout your workday. It’s discounted to $39.99 for Amazon Prime Big Deal Days.

The Govee Glide Hexa Light Panels are a simple and fun way to add some personality to your work desk setup without taking up any actual desk space. The hexagon-shaped panels mount on the wall behind your monitor and can display different colors and customizable lighting effects through the Govee app .

They can be used to create a focused atmosphere during work hours and can be switched to more dynamic effects when gaming or taking a break. The panels can be arranged in different patterns to match your style.

These are 44% off at Amazon for Prime Big Deal Days, now $99.99 .

If you’re someone who hasn’t yet delved into the world of fidget toys but often finds yourself playing with random objects or even wrappers during calls or meetings, Speks might be for you. They’re tiny magnets that you can fidget or build with to keep your brain focused and your hands busy.

Instead of fidgeting with whatever happens to be within reach, you can have something that is actually made for the job and is more satisfying to have in your hands. They can help you stay focused and relieve stress throughout your workday.

This post originally published July 5 and has been updated with additional products, and to reflect new pricing and discounts .

articles.body: Representing Paradox’s Squad, Dhadkan aka Daksh Pendharker from Sonipat has emerged as the winner of Hustle 5 – Apna Homeground, taking home the coveted title and the grand prize of Rs 1 crore after weeks of hard-hitting performances, fierce competition and unforgettable hip-hop moments. WhysoKai secured the first runner-up position, while Harmeet finished as the second runner-up.Led by Rap Supremo Badshah, rooted in the spirit of Apna Homeground, Hustle 5 celebrated India’s diverse hip-hop culture, bringing together contestants and Squad Bosses who represented distinct sounds, stories and journeys. From standout performances to special appearances and hard-hitting bars, Hustle 5 – Apna Homeground celebrated the voices shaping India’s hip-hop culture, ending the season with Dhadkan taking home the ultimate win.Reflecting on his journey, Dhadkan, aka Daksh, expressed, “It still feels unreal jab bhi main sochta hoon ki ek time pe maine apni notes mein is moment ko manifest kiya tha… and cut to the winner of Hustle Season 5 is Dhadkan! Yeh journey has been nothing short of crazy, full of new experiences, learnings and a beautiful new family. Special thanks to Badshah Bhai, Squad bosses and the entire production, music, and PR teams, along with everyone who has played a huge part in this journey. I feel truly blessed to have been a part of this season, which was an ode to Homeground. And dil se thank you to everyone, especially the audience, for accepting me and giving me so much love. This is Dhadkan signing off from Hustle 5 par asli safar toh ab shuru hua hai!”On Dhadkan’s victory, Paradox added, “Seeing Dhadkan lift the trophy is a proud moment and a reminder of how much talent and hard work this season has brought to the stage. Every artist on Hustle 5 – Apna Homeground has had their own journey and Dhadkan has truly made his mark with his performances and dedication. It’s great to see him take home the title and I’m excited to see his journey grow and what he does next with this prize money and the opportunities that come with it.”Rap Supremo Badshah said, “Every season of Hustle unearths authentic voices, but Dhadkan’s run on Hustle 5 – Apna Homeground has been exceptional right from the start. Winning this season and taking home Rs 1 crore is well deserved and I hope this is just the beginning of bigger things for him.
